# Phase 2B Context: H-M2
## Pile-Trained Models Develop Measurable Memorization of Repeated Benchmark-Adjacent Patterns

**Generated by:** Phase 2C Step 1 (JIT from 02b_verification_plan.md)
**Date:** 2026-08-25
**Hypothesis ID:** H-M2
**Type:** MECHANISM
**Gate:** SHOULD_WORK
**Prerequisites:** H-M1 (VALIDATED)

---

## Hypothesis Statement

Under the setting of Pythia Pile and dedup-Pile models at token-count-matched checkpoints, if Pile training corpus contains repeated documents with benchmark n-gram overlap, then Pile-trained models will show detectably higher min-k% probability scores on benchmark test items compared to dedup-Pile models, because repeated exposure to near-duplicate content encoding benchmark test patterns drives near-memorization of those patterns.

---

## Experimental Setup (from Phase 2A via Phase 2B)

### Dataset
- **Name:** Pythia Pile/dedup-Pile pretraining checkpoints + MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, WinoGrande (standard benchmark test sets)
- **Type:** standard
- **Source:** EleutherAI/pythia on HuggingFace; benchmark test sets via lm-evaluation-harness
- **Path:** huggingface.co/EleutherAI/pythia-*; benchmarks via lm-evaluation-harness
- **Hypothesis Fit:** Pile vs dedup-Pile provides exact controlled curation comparison. The 4 benchmarks cover knowledge-intensive (MMLU, ARC) and reasoning-intensive (HellaSwag, WinoGrande) tasks. Full test sets (≥500 items per benchmark) provide sufficient power for min-k% probability scoring.

### Model
- **Name:** Pythia-1B and Pythia-6.9B (both Pile and dedup-Pile variants at token-count-matched checkpoints)
- **Type:** Decoder-only GPT-NeoX
- **Source:** EleutherAI/pythia on HuggingFace
- **Hypothesis Fit:** Same architecture across curation variants; 154 intermediate checkpoints enable token-count matching; 1B and 6.9B chosen for statistical power and to check scale interaction.

---

## Variables

- **Independent:** Training corpus (Pile with repetitions vs dedup-Pile without)
- **Dependent:** Min-k% probability score on benchmark test items
- **Controlled:** Model size (1B and 6.9B), checkpoint matched by token count, min-k% implementation (Shi et al. 2023 reference)

---

## Verification Protocol

1. Load Pythia-1B and Pythia-6.9B (Pile and dedup-Pile) at token-count-matched checkpoints
2. Apply Shi et al. 2023 min-k% method to all benchmark test items (MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC, WinoGrande — full test sets, ≥500 items per benchmark)
3. Compute per-item min-k% probability; aggregate mean per benchmark per model
4. Compare Pile vs dedup-Pile min-k% scores using paired t-test; apply Bonferroni correction across 4 benchmarks (α = 0.0125)
5. Check if high-contamination benchmarks (from H-M1) show larger memorization signal difference than low-contamination benchmarks

---

## Success Criteria

- **Primary:** Pile models show significantly higher min-k% probability on ≥2 benchmarks vs dedup-Pile (p < 0.0125)
- **Secondary:** Magnitude of memorization difference correlates with benchmark contamination level from H-M1

---

## Failure Response

- IF fails: EXPLORE — min-k% may not capture near-memorization (vs verbatim); try alternative memorization metrics or document similarity approaches

---

## Key References

- Shi et al. 2023 — Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models (min-k% probability method)
- Biderman et al. 2023 — Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models (Pile vs dedup-Pile checkpoints)
- Lee et al. 2022 — Deduplicating Training Data Makes LMs Better
